notes.decision: Preserved as-is in both Coptic and English. This appears to function as a chapter-number marker (the standard Kephalaia layout shows a centered chapter symbol on its own line, repeated in the heading line). The Coptic letter-form ⲙⲫ does not parse as a standard alphabetic numeral (where 48 would be ⲙⲏ); it may be a scribal glyph or an idiosyncratic chapter notation. The same pattern reappears at line 25 with ⲛ̄ for the next chapter.

Translated as 'questioned' / 'answered' / 'said' depending on subject (disciples / Illuminator / Apostle). The form recurs five times on this page (lines 3, 8, 32, 34) as a discourse-introducer, parallel to the well-attested ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ 'he said' in line 28. May be a Lycopolitan variant of a verb of speech (possibly built on Greek τάσσω 'arrange, declare' or a contraction of ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'request'). Functions consistently as 'addressed/responded to.'
Rendered 'saying: Indeed.' ⲡⲓⲫⲉ likely a Lycopolitan formation related to ⲡⲉϫⲉ-/ⲡⲉϫⲁ⸗ ('say') functioning as direct-speech introducer; ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛ = ⲙ̄ⲙⲟⲛ 'indeed, truly' affirmative particle.

Translated 'they have not pierced them.' Negative perfect ⲙⲡⲉ- + verb + 3pl object. ϣⲁⲧⲟⲩ likely from ϣⲱⲧ/ϣⲁⲧ 'pierce, cut, wound.' The disciples ask how the Wheel turns over the heavens stretched between winds and earth without piercing them.

Translated 'they do not mingle.' Lycopolitan negative habitual + reduplicated verb of mingling, related to ⲗⲱⲃϣ 'mingle, blend' (in glossary). The reduplication ϩⲗⲁⲙⲗⲙ̄ / ϣⲟⲗⲁⲙⲗⲙ̄ / ⲟⲗⲁⲙⲗⲙ̄ recurs throughout the passage as the technical term for cosmic non-interpenetration.
Translated 'as it courses.' From ⲥⲓⲧⲉ/ⲥⲓϯ 'shoot, throw, run, course' — apt for the astronomical motion of the cosmic Wheel through the heavens.
Greek ἐπειδή 'since, because' with Lycopolitan vocalic shift. Standard causal connector.

Rendered as 'the figurehead ... the head, at the front of the ship.' ⲕⲟⲟⲍ (= ⲕⲟⲟϩ 'corner, edge, prow') with ⲧⲁⲡ 'head' = the prow figurehead. ⲁⲣⲭⲏ here is spatial 'front, foremost part' rather than temporal. ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ = 'the ship' (cf. ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲏ 'ship of the night' in glossary) given the maritime simile context.
Tentatively rendered 'habitually.' Possibly ϣⲁⲩ-(ⲕⲱⲛ?) habitual auxiliary or a discourse-marker introducing customary action. Etymology unclear; flagged for parallels.
Translated 'cleaves.' Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲱϣ 'split, divide' or ⲡⲱⲱⲛⲉ 'turn, divide.' Fits the prow-cleaving-waves imagery.
Rendered 'before delay comes.' ⲉⲙⲡⲧⲁⲧⲉ = ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ 'before' (negative temporal); ⲱⲥⲕ = ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, delay' (in glossary). The waves rejoin behind the prow in an instant.
Translated 'upon their head.' ⲍⲓ- 'upon' + ⲡⲧⲁⲍ-ⲟⲩ 'their head/forehead' (Lyc. ⲧⲁⲡ with prosthetic and 3pl suffix). Refers to the topmost point of the ship/figurehead where the parted waves rejoin.

Translated 'a bird that ascends out from the air.' ⲍⲁⲗⲏⲧ = ϩⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'bird' (in glossary as ⲡⲍⲁⲗⲏⲧ); ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲗⲉ = ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'ascend, mount.' The bird's flight leaves no visible track in the air — the second simile of cosmic non-interference.

Rendered 'the manner of the men in the sun.' Reads ⲡⲓⲥⲙⲁⲧ as 'this manner/likeness' with the men/figures depicted on/within the sun-ship — a third comparison: cosmic figures move through the heavens without leaving discoverable track. Alternative reading 'this likeness of men' equally possible.

Translated 'they do not cut their path.' Negative habitual ⲙⲁ- + ⲕⲟⲡ (possibly from a verb of cutting/marking) + ⲡⲟⲩ-ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ 'their path.' The cosmic figures leave no carved/recognizable track behind them.
